summary: Ferrous sulfate is an over-the-counter oral iron supplement providing 65 mg of elemental iron per 325 mg tablet, used to prevent or treat iron deficiency. It is best taken after meals to limit GI upset. A boxed-style warning highlights that accidental iron overdose is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under 6, so products must be kept out of reach of children.

moa: Iron is an essential component of hemoglobin, myoglobin, and several enzymes. Supplemental ferrous (Fe2+) iron is absorbed in the duodenum and proximal jejunum and is incorporated into hemoglobin, correcting iron-deficiency anemia and replenishing depleted iron stores.

absolute: Iron-overload states (e.g. hemochromatosis, hemosiderosis) - not for self-treatment
relative: Anemia not yet evaluated by a clinician
Active GI ulceration or inflammatory bowel disease

preg: If you are pregnant, seek the advice of a health professional before using this product. Oral iron is widely used to prevent and treat iron deficiency in pregnancy; the OTC label advises professional guidance before use.
lact: If you are nursing a baby, seek the advice of a health professional before using this product.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is provided in the OTC labeling; treatment of anemia should be supervised by a doctor.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is provided in the OTC labeling; treatment of anemia should be supervised by a doctor.

major: Oral tetracycline antibiotics - iron interferes with absorption; separate doses by at least 2 hours
moderate: Antacids and acid-reducing agents - reduce iron absorption
Fluoroquinolone antibiotics - chelation reduces antibiotic absorption (separate dosing)
Levothyroxine - reduced absorption when taken together
interactions.food: Food (especially with calcium) reduces iron absorption but lessens GI upset; vitamin C may enhance absorption
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction noted in the labeling
interactions.diagnostics: May cause black stools and can produce false-positive results on occult-blood tests

emergency: Accidental overdose in a child - contact a Poison Control Center immediately

missed: Take the missed dose when you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip it and resume your usual schedule; do not double up.
overdose: Accidental overdose of iron-containing products is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under 6. In case of accidental overdose, call a doctor or Poison Control Center (1-800-222-1222) immediately. Keep out of reach of children.
